text:
Mira: FYI I started a small cleanup PR for the optkit migration guide. Moves batching examples into examples/batching/v2 and consolidates kv-prefetch notes. PR #5010
Carlos: Nice. Any breaking link fallout in the staging preview?
Mira: The build is mostly green but linkcheck flagged 8 broken links pointing at the old /optimize/batch_examples paths.
Priya: Can you paste the top 3 so I can triage?
Mira: Sure: 
- /optimize/batch_examples/README.md (now examples/batching/README.md)
- /optimize/kv_prefetch.md (split into examples/kv-prefetch.md + snippets/kv-usage.py)
- /optimize/quant_profiles/standard (moved to optkit/quant-profiles/standard.md)

Samir: We should avoid manual redirects for each file. Suggest a short mapping file and a docs plugin that looks up old -> new during Sphinx build. I'll sketch a minimal YAML in docs/_data/legacy_to_optkit.yml
Priya: That works. Also, we have external links inside SDK snippets referencing the old paths. We need to update those in src/snippets/python and src/snippets/js. I can run a sed script and open a PR.
Carlos: If you do sed, include a unit that asserts the snippet file still renders in docs build. I can add a CI job that runs a light Sphinx build on changed snippets.
Mira: Good call. I'll add a note in the PR description: "do not delete originals until redirects are live".
Samir: Draft mapping example:
```yaml
- from: "optimize/batch_examples/README.md"
  to: "examples/batching/README.md"
- from: "optimize/kv_prefetch.md"
  to: "examples/kv-prefetch.md"
- from: "optimize/quant_profiles/standard"
  to: "optkit/quant-profiles/standard.md"
```
Priya: I'll update the python snippets to import the new example module path and leave a one-line comment pointing to the new canonical doc. PR by EOD.
Carlos: I'll own the CI validator change (docs-ci/snippet-check). Will add a lightweight check that runs sphinx-build -nW on the snippet subset. Expect a follow-up PR tomorrow.
Mira: Quick note on anchors: some product teams linked to anchors like /optimize/quant_profiles/standard#float16. We can't reliably preserve every anchor name. Suggest we implement a small client-side anchor fallback handler that attempts to map old anchor tokens to the new ones via a short JSON table.
Samir: Yep I can produce the small anchors.json and add the JS that looks up legacy anchors and scrolls to the new fragment. Low friction.
Priya: Also: update the SDK examples README to mention the migration and include example import diffs. That will save a lot of cross-team confusion.
Mira: Plan checklist:
- Samir: add mapping YAML + anchors.json + docs build hook to consult mapping (PR today)
- Priya: sed/patch snippets in python/js + add inline comments (PR today)
- Carlos: add docs-ci snippet check (PR tomorrow morning)
- Mira: update PR description and run a fresh staging preview after merges

docssys-bot: Staging preview: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/optkit/preview/5010 (8 link errors) :warning:

Carlos: We can split the 8 across the three PRs. I expect 3 fixed by Priya, 4 by Samir, 1 remaining for Mira to map anchors.
Samir: I'll include the mapping generator script so we can re-run linkcheck easily.
Priya: Heads-up: one snippet references the old python package layout (redwood.optimize.prefetch). New import is redwood.optkit.prefetch. I'll fix imports and add a deprecation comment in the snippet.
Mira: Thanks. If the redirects are in place we can keep the old URLs for 2 weeks and then schedule deletion in a follow-up cleanup CHORE.
Carlos: Sounds good. Please ping #integrations if the docs-ci job starts failing after the template change.
Mira: Thanks all. Posting a follow-up with the grep output and the exact sed commands in ~10m.
